(sec-item-objectcontactconvexconvex)=
# ObjectContactConvexConvex

A penalty contact between two convex polytopes, each given by its points and the triangles of its surface in the frame of its marker; up to 8 contact points carry an edge or a face of contact. Contact law and friction as for ObjectContactSphereTriangle.

Author: Gerstmayr Johannes

## Interface

- Nodes it takes: [](#sec-item-nodegenericdata)
- Markers it acts on: those providing `Position` and `Orientation`: [](#sec-item-markerbodyrigid), [](#sec-item-markernoderigid), [](#sec-item-markersuperelementrigid), [](#sec-item-markerkinematictreerigid), [](#sec-item-markerbodyuser)

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'ContactConvexConvex':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | connector's unique name |
| **markerNumbers** | ArrayMarkerIndex | 2 | [ invalid (-1), invalid (-1) ] | (symbol: $[m0,m1]\tp$) list of markers: the frames of shape 0 and shape 1, in which their points are given |
| **nodeNumber** | NodeIndex |  | invalid (-1) | (symbol: $n_d$) node number of a NodeGenericData with numberOfDataCoordinates = 24, needed for the discontinuous iteration (friction and contact): a block of 3 for each of the up to 8 contact points $i$ holds the values of the last PostNewton iteration: data[3i] the gap, data[3i+1] the norm of the tangential velocity (stick or slip), data[3i+2] the impact velocity; with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 a block of 4, the fourth the plastic overlap |
| **points0** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\LU{m0}{\pv}_{0,i}$) the points of shape 0 in the frame of marker 0, rows of 3 coordinates; shape 0 is their convex hull |
| **triangles0** | NumpyMatrixI |  | [] | the triangles of the surface of shape 0, rows of 3 indices into points0, ordered so that the normal points out of the shape; checked at Assemble |
| **points1** | NumpyMatrix |  | [] | (symbol: $\LU{m1}{\pv}_{1,i}$) the points of shape 1 in the frame of marker 1, rows of 3 coordinates; shape 1 is their convex hull |
| **triangles1** | NumpyMatrixI |  | [] | the triangles of the surface of shape 1, rows of 3 indices into points1, ordered so that the normal points out of the shape; checked at Assemble |
| **dynamicFriction** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\mu_d$) dynamic friction coefficient for friction model, see StribeckFunction in exudyn.physics, [](#sec-module-physics) |
| **frictionProportionalZone** | UReal |  | 0.001 | (symbol: $v_{reg}$) limit velocity [m/s] up to which the friction is proportional to velocity (for regularization / avoid numerical oscillations), see StribeckFunction in exudyn.physics (named regVel there!), [](#sec-module-physics) |
| **contactStiffness** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $k_c$) normal contact stiffness [SI:N/m] (units in case that $n_\mathrm{exp}=1$) |
| **contactDamping** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $d_c$) linear normal contact damping [SI:N/(m s)]; this damping should be used (!=0) if the restitution coefficient is < 1, as it changes its behavior. |
| **contactStiffnessExponent** | PReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $n_\mathrm{exp}$) exponent in normal contact model [SI:1] |
| **contactPlasticityRatio** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\lambda_\mathrm{P}$) ratio of contact stiffness for first loading and unloading/reloading [SI:1] of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model, as in ObjectContactSphereSphere, with impactModel Linear: unloading and reloading with $K_2 = k_c/(1-\lambda_\mathrm{P})$ from the plastic overlap $\lambda_\mathrm{P}\,\delta_{max}$ of the contact; 0: the elastic law; not 0: each contact point has a block of 4 data coordinates, the fourth the plastic overlap (#3336) |
| **adhesionCoefficient** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $k_\mathrm{adh}$) coefficient for adhesion [SI:N/m] (units in case that $n_\mathrm{adh}=1$) of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model; used with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 |
| **adhesionExponent** | UReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $n_\mathrm{adh}$) exponent for adhesion coefficient [SI:1] of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model |
| **constantPullOffForce** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $f_\mathrm{adh}$) constant adhesion force [SI:N] of each contact point in contact, of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model; used with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 |
| **restitutionCoefficient** | PReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $e_\mathrm{res}$) coefficient of restitution [SI:1]; used in particular for impact mechanics; different models available within parameter impactModel; the coefficient must be > 0, but can become arbitrarily small to emulate plastic impact (however very small values may lead to numerical problems) |
| **minimumImpactVelocity** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\dot\delta_\mathrm{-,min}$) minimal impact velocity for coefficient of restitution [SI:1]; this value adds a lower bound for impact velocities for calculation of viscous impact force; it can be used to apply a larger damping behavior for low impact velocities (or permanent contact) |
| **impactModel** | ContactImpactModel |  | ContactImpactModel.Linear | (symbol: $m_\mathrm{impact}$) the impact model, see ContactImpactModel: Linear (only the linear contactDamping), HuntCrossley or GonthierCarvalhoMartins, the latter much more accurate regarding the coefficient of restitution in the full range (0, 1]; the integers 0, 1, 2 are accepted as well; in all models, the linear contactDamping is added, if not set to zero (#3327) |
| **activeConnector** | Bool |  | True | flag, which determines, if the connector is active; used to deactivate (temporarily) a connector or constraint |
| **contactForceUserFunction** | ObjectContactConvexConvexContactForceUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\mathrm{UF} \in \Rcal^3$) A Python function which replaces the contact law and returns the contact force on marker 0, while the item computes the geometry and the contact state; the contact parameters of the item are then not used; see description below (#3324) |
| **visualization** | VObjectContactConvexConvex |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

## Visualization parameters

The parameters of `VObjectContactConvexConvex`, given as `visualization`:

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **show** | Bool |  | False | set true, if item is shown in visualization and false if it is not shown; draws the triangles of both shapes with the contact settings |
| **color** | Float4 | 4 | [0.7,0.7,0.7,1.] | RGBA connector color; if R==-1, use default color |

## Drawing

Drawn as [all connectors](#sec-drawing-objectsconnector); the triangles of both shapes with `contact.showTriangles`.

Settings beyond those of all connectors: [`contact.colorTriangles`](#sec-vsettingscontact), [`contact.showTriangles`](#sec-vsettingscontact).

## Output variables

Available as `OutputVariableType` in sensors, `Get...Output()` and other functions:

```{tabularcolumns} \Y{0.25}\Y{0.25}\Y{0.5}
```

| output variable | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| Distance |  | the signed distance of the two shapes, the gap (< 0: penetration), from the current configuration, also with activeConnector = False |
| Position |  | the center of the contact points weighted by their normal forces; without contact force the middle of the closest points |
| Displacement |  | global vector from the closest point of shape 0 to that of shape 1 |
| Velocity |  | velocity of the body of marker 1 relative to that of marker 0 at Position |
| DisplacementLocal |  | 1D Vector, containing only gap |
| Director1 |  | the contact normal, the unit vector from shape 0 towards shape 1 |
| Force |  | global contact force on marker 0, the sum of the contact points; marker 1 gets its negative |
| Torque |  | global torque of the contact forces on marker 0, about its position |

(description-objectcontactconvexconvex)=
## Detailed description

### Definition of quantities

| intermediate variables | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| marker m0, m1 positions | $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}$, $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m1}$ | the origins of the frames of the two shapes |
| marker m0, m1 orientations | $\LU{0,m0}{\Rot}$, $\LU{0,m1}{\Rot}$ | the rotations of the frames of the two shapes |
| marker velocities | $\LU{0}{\vv}_{m0}$, $\LU{0}{\vv}_{m1}$, $\LU{0}{\tomega}_{m0}$, $\LU{0}{\tomega}_{m1}$ | global velocities and angular velocities |
| data coordinates | $\xv=[x_0,\,\ldots,\,x_{23}]\tp$ | for contact point $i$: the gap ($3i$), the norm of the tangential velocity ($3i+1$), the impact velocity ($3i+2$) |

### Geometric relations

Shape $i$ is the convex hull of its points `points`$i$, given in the frame of marker $i$; the triangles
`triangles`$i$ - the indices of three points each, ordered so that their normal points out of the shape - are its
surface, used for the contact points and for drawing. The signed distance $g$ of the two shapes - the output
Distance -, the closest points - the deepest points of a penetration - and the unit normal $\LU{0}{\nv}$ from shape
0 to shape 1 are computed by GJK and, for a penetration, EPA, the functions of `exudyn.cUtilities.Distance` with
shapes of the type Points.

An edge or a face of contact is carried by up to 8 contact points $k$:

- where $-\LU{0}{\nv}$ is the outward normal of a face of shape 1 - its triangles with this normal -, every point of
shape 0 over that face (projected along the normal into one of its triangles) is a contact point, with the
gap $g_k = -\LU{0}{\nv}\tp (\LU{0}{\pv}_k - \LU{0}{\pv}_F)$ to the plane of the face through its point
$\LU{0}{\pv}_F$;
- where $\LU{0}{\nv}$ is the outward normal of a face of shape 0, every point of shape 1 over that face, the same
way; for a face on a face, both, without the points that coincide;
- of more than 8 points the 8 deepest; otherwise the closest points of GJK and EPA, one point: an edge on an edge,
a vertex on an edge.

The contact point is the middle of the points on both shapes, $\LU{0}{\pv}_{c,k}$, and the relative velocity there
is that of the body of marker 1 relative to that of marker 0.

### Connector forces

For each contact point, the normal force - from the penetration $\delta_k = -g_k$, with `contactStiffness`
$k_c$, the exponent $n_\mathrm{exp}$, `contactDamping` $d_c$ and the impact model `impactModel` with the
restitution coefficient - and the regularized dry friction with $\mu_d$ and `frictionProportionalZone` are
computed as for `ObjectContactSphereSphere`, see [](#sec-item-objectcontactspheresphere), with the normal
and the relative velocity at the contact point; the stiffness is that of each point, so a box on its face is held by
its 4 corners. The force $\LU{0}{\fv}_k$ acts on marker 0 at the contact point, with the torque
$(\LU{0}{\pv}_{c,k} - \LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}) \times \LU{0}{\fv}_k$, and $-\LU{0}{\fv}_k$ on marker 1; the outputs Force and
Torque are their sums on marker 0. The data coordinates of each point hold its gap, tangential velocity and impact
velocity of the last post Newton step, which decide on contact and on the friction regime during the Newton
iterations (active set).

**Userfunction**: `contactForceUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, gap, gap_t, normal, tangentialVelocity, impactVelocity)`
A user function which replaces the contact law: it computes the contact force from the gap, its rate, the
contact normal, the tangential relative velocity and the impact velocity, while the item computes the geometry and
the contact state (#3324). It is called for each contact point in contact, as its block of the data node from the
last post Newton step says, and returns the force of that point.
The force is the one on marker 0 at the contact point, the convention of the output variable Force; marker 1 gets
its negative. A penetration $\delta = -g$ pushes marker 0 against the normal: the normal force $f_N > 0$ gives
$-f_N\, \nv$; a friction force on marker 0 acts along the tangential velocity.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs in which underlying item is defined |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs, allowing easy access to all object data via mbs.GetObjectParameter(itemNumber, ...) |
| `gap` | Real | $g$, the signed gap, negative in contact |
| `gap_t` | Real | $\dot g$, its rate: the relative velocity along the normal, negative while approaching |
| `normal` | Vector3D | $\LU{0}{\nv}$, the unit contact normal from marker 0 towards marker 1 (the output Director1) |
| `tangentialVelocity` | Vector3D | $\LU{0}{\vv}_t$, the velocity of the body of marker 1 relative to that of marker 0 at the contact point, normal to $\LU{0}{\nv}$ |
| `impactVelocity` | Real | the velocity of approach at the last impact, from the data node, for impact models |
| **return value** | Vector3D | the global contact force on marker 0, a list or numpy array of 3 values |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

*Example*:

```python
#the linear contact law with regularized friction as a user function: the same as contactStiffness, contactDamping,
#dynamicFriction and frictionProportionalZone of the item
def UFcontact(mbs, t, itemNumber, gap, gap_t, normal, tangentialVelocity, impactVelocity):
    k, d, mu, vReg = 1e5, 1e3, 0.3, 1e-3
    fN = -k*gap - d*gap_t                       #normal force, > 0 in compression
    vt = tangentialVelocity
    vtNorm = (vt[0]**2 + vt[1]**2 + vt[2]**2)**0.5
    fT = mu*fN/max(vtNorm, vReg)                #regularized Coulomb friction
    return [-fN*normal[i] + fT*vt[i] for i in range(3)]

mbs.AddObject(ObjectContactConvexConvex(markerNumbers=[mCube, mGround], nodeNumber=nData, points0=points0, triangles0=triangles0,
              points1=points1, triangles1=triangles1, contactForceUserFunction=UFcontact))
```

(miniexample-objectcontactconvexconvex)=
## Mini example


```python
#a cube of edge 0.2 dropped onto a fixed box, lying on its face
def Box(size):
    points = [[sx*size[0]/2, sy*size[1]/2, sz*size[2]/2] for sz in [-1,1] for sy in [-1,1] for sx in [-1,1]]
    triangles = [[0,2,1],[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[5,7,6],[0,1,4],[1,5,4],[2,6,3],[3,6,7],[0,4,2],[2,4,6],[1,3,5],[3,7,5]]
    return points, triangles
inertia = InertiaCuboid(density=1000, sideLengths=[0.2,0.2,0.2])
node = mbs.AddNode(NodeRigidBodyEP(referenceCoordinates=[0,0,0.31]+eulerParameters0))
cube = mbs.AddObject(ObjectRigidBody(nodeNumber=node, mass=inertia.Mass(), inertia=inertia.GetInertia6D()))
mbs.AddLoad(LoadMassProportional(markerNumber=mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyMass(bodyNumber=cube)), loadVector=[0,0,-9.81]))
mCube = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyRigid(bodyNumber=cube, localPosition=[0,0,0]))
mGround = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyRigid(bodyNumber=oGround, localPosition=[0,0,0]))
nData = mbs.AddNode(NodeGenericData(numberOfDataCoordinates=24, initialCoordinates=[0]*24))
points0, triangles0 = Box([0.2,0.2,0.2])
points1, triangles1 = Box([1,1,0.4])
mbs.AddObject(ObjectContactConvexConvex(markerNumbers=[mCube, mGround], nodeNumber=nData, points0=points0, triangles0=triangles0,
                                        points1=points1, triangles1=triangles1, contactStiffness=1e5, contactDamping=1e3))

mbs.Assemble()
simulationSettings = exu.SimulationSettings()
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.numberOfSteps = 1000
mbs.SolveDynamic(simulationSettings)

#at rest on its 4 lower corners: 0.2 + 0.1 - m*g/(4*k)
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.GetNodeOutput(node, exu.OutputVariableType.Position)[2]
```
